name: Concert Harp
shortDescription: 47-string pedal harp with pillar-resonator-neck triangle producing a cascading harmonic palette.
description: The concert harp is a triangular frame chordophone with 47 strings spanning six and a half octaves. Seven pedals (one per pitch class) rotate discs in the neck that shorten strings by a semitone or tone, enabling full chromatic modulation. Each string is individually tuned and plucked, coupling energy through the soundboard into the resonator box.
historicalOrigins: The double-action pedal harp was developed by Sébastien Érard in Paris in 1810, enabling modulation to any key. Ancient harps appear in Mesopotamian art from 3000 BCE.
acousticPrinciples: Each string obeys Mersenne's law: longer, heavier lower strings and shorter lighter upper strings
Pedal discs act as movable nuts, changing effective string length to raise pitch by semitone or tone
Soundboard amplifies vibration through a similar mechanism to the guitar
Short decay (no sustain pedal) creates the characteristic 'glissando' blend of notes

characteristics.timbralColor: Clear, resonant, shimmering; bright upper register, warm lower octaves
characteristics.orchestralRole: Glissando effects, arpeggiated chords, solo melodic voice, orchestral colour

soundDNA.exciter: Finger tip plucking individual gut or nylon/steel strings
soundDNA.resonator: Wooden resonator box (soundboard + enclosed air cavity)
soundDNA.harmonics: Clean harmonic series; shorter upper strings are brighter with faster decay
soundDNA.attackDecay: Fast pluck attack; exponential decay (0.5–8s depending on register)
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Clear, bell-like upper register; warm, resonant bass
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Forward radiation from soundboard; omnidirectional at lower frequencies

resonator.label: Resonator Box
resonator.function: Hollow wooden body amplifies string vibration through soundboard and enclosed air cavity.

soundboard.label: Spruce Soundboard
soundboard.function: Front face of resonator directly driven by string vibration through the string anchor points.

neck.label: Curved Neck
neck.function: Curved wooden neck housing pedal disc mechanisms that control string length.

characteristics.material: Laminated maple with brass disc mechanisms
characteristics.role: Structural top beam and pitch modulation

pillar.label: Pillar Column
pillar.function: Load-bearing column resisting the total string tension of approximately 1000 kg combined.

characteristics.material: Carved maple with internal pedal rod channels
characteristics.mechanism: Hollow column transmits pedal rod force

strings.label: String Array (47 strings)
strings.function: 47 individually-tuned strings spanning C1 to G#7. Colour-coded: C=red, F=black.

pedals.label: Seven Pedals
pedals.function: Double-action pedals in three notched positions (flat/natural/sharp) for full chromatic control.

characteristics.material: Metal foot pedals with pivot mechanism
characteristics.mechanism: Rod linkage rotates disc in neck to shorten strings

followTheSound.title: String Pluck
followTheSound.explanation: Finger tip plucks individual string, releasing stored elastic energy as transverse wave.

followTheSound.title: Disc Mechanism (Pedal Pitch)
followTheSound.explanation: Pedal-actuated discs in the neck shorten the vibrating string length by semitone or tone.

followTheSound.title: Soundboard Radiation
followTheSound.explanation: String vibration drives the spruce soundboard into flexural modes radiating sound forward.

followTheSound.title: Cavity Amplification
followTheSound.explanation: Resonator box body and air cavity amplify and colour the fundamental and harmonics.
